human_tolerance.notes: Breeds in brushy forest edges, open deciduous woods, second growth and farmland (Wikipedia). light_max is judgement: no light-tolerance source was checked. Not documented as a regular garden or urban breeder in the sources used here.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Summer residence in the United States. Nest building is limited to May through August in the behaviour program; see provenance for the derivation.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Winters in Mexico, Central America, the West Indies and northern South America; only occasional winter records in southern Florida. Migration is in April-May and September-October.

vocalizations.description: High-pitched buzzed sweet-sweet chew-chew sweet-sweet song, two to four seconds, sung by males from exposed perches (posts, wires, bush tops) to mark territory and attract females.
Sharp chip! call given by both sexes, used as an alarm when a nest or chick is threatened.

range.note: Derived from Wikipedia's Distribution section: breeding from southern Canada, south to northern Florida and eastern Texas, west to southern Nevada; winter range from southern Florida and central Mexico south through the West Indies and Central America. Native list reduced to US, CA and MX; Central American and Caribbean winter countries are omitted from this list.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Authored: Wikipedia states ground foraging and flight but no gait names. Hop is the gait the species' program uses for ground feeding; not a sourced statement.

traits.nest_type.note: Breeding section: a nest of leaves, grasses, stems and bark, bound with spider web, in dense shrub or low tree 0.3-1 m up. 'Cup' is the schema mapping for that open nest.

traits.perching.note: Sings from elevated perches (posts, wires, bush tops).

traits.size_class.note: Derived from mass_kg per schema thresholds (validator checks it).

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 14.69 g (Dunning 2008) converted to kg. Wikipedia gives an average of 14.5 g, consistent.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Wikipedia: reported range 11.2-21.4 g, converted to kg.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's Description range 11.5-15 cm (13.25 cm), converted to m. Lead gives 11.5-13 cm.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 18-23 cm wingspan range, converted to m.

traits.lifespan_y.note: DERIVED PROXY, low confidence. Input: Scholer et al. 2020 row 233, wild adult annual survival S = 0.493 (Desante et al. 2015; mark-recapture; United States; MAPS). Calculation: mean lifespan under constant annual adult survival, 1/-ln(S) = 1.41 years, rounded to 1.4. Assumptions: adult survival is constant with age; first-year mortality is excluded (not checked), which would lower this figure. Alternative input: Wikipedia cites a Hillsborough NC banding survival of 0.585 (Blake 1967), which gives 1/-ln(0.585) = 1.87 years and is not used. The 13 years 3 months oldest-record statement is a maximum and is not a typical lifespan.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits diet for the species: Diet-Seed 100, Diet-Inv 0 (certainty C). OPEN CONFLICT: Wikipedia Diet section says insects and spiders dominate breeding-season diet and seeds dominate winter. The record keeps the dataset value; the behaviour program feeds on invertebrates May-August and seed otherwise. Reviewers should decide whether to change this field.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia: solitary feeder in the breeding season, flocks with other buntings in winter. group_size [1,2] is authored judgement; winter flocking is not represented.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Judgement: sings in daylight and dawn; migrates at night (Wikipedia). Diurnal is the schema mapping for daytime activity.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: flight to shrub or tree cover; the chip! alarm call is sourced from Wikipedia.

habitat.use.note: Derived from EltonTraits ForStrat percentages: ground 40 -> 0.4; arboreal 60 = understory 40 + midhigh 20 (canopy and aerial 0).

habitat.resources.note: Resource tags from Wikipedia: forages on ground or in trees or shrubs; insects in breeding season; grass seeds in winter; dense shrub or low tree nest sites. Weights and month windows are authored judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Habitat section: brushy forest edges, second growth. Judgement for shrub_thicket.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Habitat section lists brushy edges, open woods, second growth and farmland. Avoider and light_max are judgement; no light or urban source checked.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia: migratory; migration April-May and September-October. Scholer row 233 migration category 'migrant'.

seasonal.phases.note: Absent phase Nov-Mar follows Wikipedia's migration window and winter range (southern Florida and Mexico south). 'nesting' May-August is AUTHORED: derived from the April-May and September-October migration windows and the breeding statement; no source gives June-August directly. Winter presence in southern Florida is not represented.

vocalizations.song.note: Song description from Wikipedia. season_months May-August is authored, matching the nesting window.

vocalizations.alarm.note: Sharp chip! call used as alarm by both sexes.

behavior.note: Species-local program bt-indigo-bunting-v1 (species/passerina-cyanea/behavior.json). Adapted from the shared bt-perching-songbird-v1 because its nest months are hard-coded to April-May. Calendar: nest, song and insect feeding enabled May, June, July and August only. Hop for ground feeding and flight for flee are authored.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description (male cerulean blue with indigo head, black wings; female brown). Proportions and mesh are authored judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Wikipedia Breeding section: incubation 12-13 days, chicks fledge 10-12 days after hatching. Egg and Adult stages are sourced; Juvenile has no duration because none was sourced.
